correctness.rationale: An independent first-step check decomposes each parent passage into a geometric number of failed child excursions and one final step. At a vertex with h children the failure count has mean h and variance h(h+1); a failed excursion chooses a uniform child and lasts 1+Z_c. Induction gives mean 2s_v−1 and the variance recurrence V_v=sum_c V_c+4sum_c s_c²+4(s_v−1)², equivalent to the frozen recurrence. Thus V_x=4s(s−1)+8sum_{v≠x}s_v(s_v−1), independent of the part beyond y. At fixed branch sizes the lower bound requires every proper descendant of a branch root to be a leaf; strict integer smoothing then gives the unique balanced size multiset. For the upper bound, induction on an unrestricted branch of size r gives maximum P(r)=(4/3)r(r−1)(2r−1), uniquely at the endpoint-rooted path: the child-size contributions F(u)=P(u)+4u(u−1) have strictly increasing increments, so concentrate all surplus on one child, and one child is best when the number is unrestricted. At x this same allocation at fixed k gives (s−k,1,…,1), including k=s−1, when all children are leaves. Substitution of s=2m+1, k=m verifies both polynomials and the ratio asymptotic m/6 with equal marked degrees, mean and order. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and verify.py without running the latter; the absorbing-chain check there is finite (s=2–8) and not needed for the proof. In its final m-loop it asserts the lower expression and U>=L rather than a separate upper-polynomial identity; the upper polynomial was checked by exact substitution above.

value.rationale: The complete sharp optimization answers how much root-degree information restricts dispersion when the mean is already fixed by the size of the starting component. The equality shapes identify two competing mechanisms, and the unbounded matched-data ratio shows that any size-independent multiplicative prediction from those statistics fails. Credit rests on the sharp constrained classification, not on rediscovering the known moment formula.
